sections.h2: What is Evans County, Georgia, and who buys homes there?
sections.html:
Evans County is the smallest of the four counties in the Census comparison by both people and land, with 183 square miles in the coastal plain and Claxton as both county seat and largest city. Voters ratified its creation on November 3, 1914, carving it from Bulloch and Tattnall counties, and Bellville, Daisy and Hagan are its other cities (Wikipedia). The Canoochee River is the main waterway, and since 2023 the county has belonged to the Statesboro micropolitan area.

The Census Bureau counted 10,774 residents in 2020 and estimated 11,028 for July 2025, up 2.3 percent. Its QuickFacts table lists a median owner-occupied home value of $138,200, median gross rent of $719 and median household income of $53,259. Owners occupy 65.4 percent of homes, and builders pulled 25 permits in 2025.

Wikipedia names Claxton Poultry Company, Valmont Newmark, the Georgia Department of Corrections, Camellia Health and Rehabilitation and Pinewood Christian Academy among major employers.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Evans County?
sections.html:
The push to form the county came from residents who wanted a closer courthouse, more office jobs and more hotels and eating places, according to Wikipedia. The Savannah and Western Railroad created stations that grew into Bellville, Claxton, Daisy and Hagan, and the current neoclassical courthouse in Claxton was completed in 1923.

In July 1940 the federal government bought land for Camp Stewart, later Fort Stewart, and an estimated 1,500 people were displaced across the counties involved. Growth followed in the late 1950s and 1960s with the Evans County Heart Study, the Claxton-Evans County Airport and, in December 1967, Evans Memorial Hospital.

sections.h2: Where do you reach the Evans County tax offices?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner works from Claxton and the Tax Assessor shares a county phone line. The commissioner's department page gives the street address and hours.

  • Tax Commissioner: 201 Freeman Street, Suite 4, Claxton; mailing address P.O. Box 685; phone 912-739-1147; open 8:15 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday.
  • County main line: 912-739-1141, option 1 for the Tax Commissioner and Tax Assessor; the county contact page lists 8:00 a.m. to noon and 1:00 to 5:00 p.m.
  • Records: parcel and exemption information appears on the assessor's qPublic pages.

The property tax FAQ asks customers to fax or email documents, since the staff is small, and notes that you can also come in to check records. That is worth following if you need a payoff before closing, because phone lines are busy around the due date.

sections.h2: When are Evans County property taxes due and what are the late charges?
sections.html:
Property taxes are due December 20 of each year, and the late-fee schedule is short. Interest of 1 percent is added each month after the due date, and a one-time 10 percent penalty applies after 90 days.

Evans County property tax FAQ: due date, late charges and lien
StepWhat the county says
Due dateDecember 20 each year
Monthly interest1 percent per month after the due date
One-time penalty10 percent after 90 days
Tax lien (fi. fa.)Placed on the Execution Docket with the Clerk of Superior Court once taxes are past due

A fi. fa. can hurt your credit for up to seven years, the county warns. Evans County's escrow rule is also spelled out: the bill is mailed to the owner and not to the mortgage company, because the commissioner has no way to know who the lienholder is. Mortgage companies request the amounts each year, and the office suggests keeping your bill for your records.

sections.h2: How do Evans County assessments and appeals work?
sections.html:
The Board of Tax Assessors values property, and an owner who disagrees with a change has 45 days from the date of the notice to appeal. The assessors' exemptions page says that if the board makes no change, the appeal moves automatically to the County Board of Equalization, and a hearing follows.

Arbitration is available in place of the board hearing, and the next step after either is superior court. The page limits appeals to three grounds:

  • Taxability of the property.
  • The value placed on it.
  • Uniformity of that value compared with similar properties.

It adds that a complaint about the amount of tax is not a valid ground, since the tax follows from the millage rate. The Georgia Department of Revenue says the appeal must be postmarked within the 45 days, so mail it early. Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value.

sections.h2: Which homestead and land programs does Evans County list?
sections.html:
Evans County takes homestead applications at the Tax Commissioner's office between January 1 and April 1, and the exemption renews automatically once granted. You must own and occupy the home on January 1, and you reapply only after a change in ownership, a name or spelling correction on the deed, or a move to a different exemption type.

The assessor's page, which still shows older income figures, describes the standard exemption at $2,000 off the 40 percent assessed value. It also lists $4,000 for owners 65 and older within an income test, a school-tax exemption up to $10,000 for owners 62 and older within an income test, and $50,000 for qualifying disabled veterans and unremarried surviving spouses. Ask the assessors for the current income limits. A tax deferral exists for owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less, and the deferred tax comes due when ownership changes.

Land has its own track. Conservation Use needs an application by April 1 with a $10 recording fee and a 10-year covenant, and a broken covenant can bring a penalty of twice the taxes saved. Freeport applications for qualifying inventory are also due April 1.

sections.h2: What should an Evans County seller do about taxes and the closing?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner in writing, then give it to your closing attorney. Past-due years come off first, and the current bill is divided in the contract.

  • Pay any fi. fa. so a lien does not appear in the title search.
  • Update the commissioner with the new owner's mailing address after the deed is recorded.
  • If the buyer has a mortgage with escrow, tell your own lender to close the escrow account.
  • Keep a copy of your warranty deed; the Clerk of Superior Court can provide recorded copies.

A land sale adds one more step. If the land is in Conservation Use, the exemption page says a buyer who continues the original use may sign the covenant and avoid a penalty, while a change in use during the ten years triggers all penalties.

sections.h2: Why might Evans County sellers choose a quick sale?
sections.html:
Only 25 building permits were issued in 2025, so most buyers are looking at existing houses. A sale to a buyer who pays cash and takes the home as is can skip repair negotiations, which helps when a tax bill or a lien is already on the parcel.

Retail sales per capita reached $21,195 in 2022, the highest among the four counties, and 22.6 percent of residents live in poverty. Hispanic or Latino residents are 13.4 percent of the population. The right route depends on how fast you need to close and how much repair work the house needs.

faqs.q: When are Evans County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due December 20 of each year, according to the county's property tax FAQ. After that date, 1 percent interest is added monthly. A 10 percent penalty is added once, after 90 days.

faqs.q: Does Evans County send the bill to my mortgage company?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner mails the bill to the owner because the office does not know who the lienholder is or whether an escrow account exists. Lenders request the amounts directly each year.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Evans County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the notice of change. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, and if no change is made the appeal goes to the Board of Equalization. Arbitration is the alternative.

faqs.q: What is a fi. fa. in Evans County?
faqs.a: A fi. fa. is a tax lien the commissioner places on the Execution Docket with the Clerk of Superior Court when taxes are past due. The county says it can affect your credit for up to seven years, so clear it before you sell.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead exemption in Evans County?
faqs.a: Apply at the Tax Commissioner's office in Claxton between January 1 and April 1. Call 912-739-1141 and press option 1. The exemption renews each year unless ownership changes.
